newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey still assessing sugar export tender.
newsitem.headline: Turkey still assessing sugar export tender.

text.p: Turkey's state sugar refinery Turkseker said on Wednesday it was still assessing bids for its 50,000-tonne whites export tender and it could be concluded early on Thursday.
A Turkseker official said it might consider splitting the offer into two or three parts.
Traders said the tender, which closed on Monday, had attracted more local company interest than international companies because of the terms.

Turkseker required that the sugar should be delivered on a free-on-truck basis to the buyer from several refineries at various locations in Turkey. The buyers should also give a letter of guarantee equal to the value of their purchase.
Traders expected the sugar to be delivered from the refineries at Elbistan, Agri, Kars, Bor and Carsamba.

They said the bidders included local food and commodities traders Lebsan, Baykur, Naptat, Yilmazlar, Rotel, Ram and Fissan, and named E D & F Man and Andre among the few international companies which participated.
They said prices from some competing local companies ran as high as a $20 premium over Paris futures.
"One company gave more than that," said one local trader.
"Several companies withdrew their bids after some aggressive local food traders, who might have good contacts with Iran and Georgia, came up real high with prices," another said.
Traders said Lebsan bid for 46,000 tonnes, Baykur 10,000 tonnes and other local companies for smaller amounts. Turkseker does not accept bids lower than 2,0000 tonnes.
